title: Minimum Window Substring
statement: You get a string s and a string target. Find the shortest stretch of neighbouring characters in s that contains every character of target, counting repeats. If no such stretch exists, return an empty string.

example.caption: BANC is the shortest stretch of s that holds an A, a B and a C.

idea.sentence: Grow the window on the right until it covers the target. Then shrink it from the left for as long as it still covers, and remember the shortest one.

jargon.plain: The window holds at least as many of each target letter as the target does. Extra letters are fine.
How many target letters, counting repeats, the window still lacks. When it hits 0 the window covers.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: s then target, e.g. "XABYCAB", "ABC"

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Try every start and end, and count letters in each stretch.

rows.name: Sliding window
rows.note: Each letter of s enters once and leaves at most once. The table holds the distinct letters of target.

fast.takeaway: Two markers only move forward. The right one finds a window that works, the left one squeezes it down to the smallest one.

stages.title: Count what is needed
stages.note: A table of target letter counts, and a single number for how many letters are still missing.

stages.title: Grow on the right
stages.note: The new letter is counted. If the window was still short of it, one fewer letter is missing.

stages.title: Shrink while covered
stages.note: While nothing is missing, drop the left letter. Stop when a needed letter leaves.

stages.title: Keep the shortest
stages.note: Each covering window is compared with the best so far. Only a strictly shorter one replaces it.

stages.title: Return the best
stages.note: Return the best stretch, or an empty string if no window ever covered the target.

edges.title: Target is the whole string
edges.why: The window covers only at the very end, and shrinking one letter breaks it.

edges.title: Repeats in target
edges.why: Target needs two a letters but s has one. Missing never reaches 0, so no window is found.

edges.title: Letter absent
edges.why: A letter that is not in s can never be covered. Return the empty string, not null.

edges.title: Shrinks past a tie
edges.why: Windows of length 5, 4, 4 and then 3 cover the target. The 3 is found only because the left marker keeps squeezing.

gotchas.text: Count repeats. target "aab" needs two a letters. A set of letters would accept a window with one a.
Shrink with a while loop, not an if. After one drop the window may still cover, and a shorter answer may follow.
Use Infinity as the initial best length, not 0. And Map.get returns undefined for letters outside target, so read it with ?? 0.
need[s[i]] on a missing key returns 0, and the -- then stores -1. That is the intended 'surplus' value, but it does mean the map also grows with letters that are not in target.
Slicing s[a:b] shares the original string's memory. Strings are immutable, so this is safe and cheap.

recap.key: Track how many target letters are missing. Grow right until none are missing, then shrink left while still none are, saving the shortest.
moves: Count target letters in need and set missing to its length
Move right. A letter still needed lowers missing
While missing is 0, record the window, then drop the left letter
Return the shortest window, or an empty string
